trial_court: Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) Sirsi, MC No.29/2006 & M.C No.8/2007
case_name: Suvarna Kom Ratnakar Shet v. Ratnakar Vinayak Shet — M.F.A.No. 23999/2009 & C W No. 24000 2009

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Suvarna Kom Ratnakar Shet, wife, bank employee
parties.respondent_defendant: Ratnakar Vinayak Shet, husband, bank employee

facts_of_case: The wife filed for judicial separation and the husband filed for divorce. The trial court granted judicial separation in favor of the wife and dismissed her petition for restitution of conjugal rights. Both cases were appealed to this court.

legal_principles.principle: Desertion is a matter of inference to be drawn from the facts and circumstances of each case.
legal_principles.held: The inference may be drawn from certain facts which may not in another case he capable of leading to the same inference: that is to say. the facts have to be viewed as to the purpose which is revealed by those acts or by conduct and expression of intention, both anterior and subsequent to the actual acts of separation.
cited_cases: BWIN CHANDER JAISINGHBHAT SHAll VS. PRABHAWATI, (1957) AIR 176

legal_principles.principle: The offence of desertion commences when the fact of separation and the animus deserendi co-exist.
legal_principles.held: The offence of desertion commences when the fact of separation and the animus deserendi co-exist. But it is not necessary that they should commence at the same time.
cited_cases: BWIN CHANDER JAISINGHBHAT SHAll VS. PRABHAWATI, (1957) AIR 176

outcome.final_order: The appeals are allowed, and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court are set aside.
